title: An honest answer without unlimited debt

captions.physics: Tying a reply to further obligation
captions.emotions: Feeling the weight of respectful words

meaning: You can preserve an honest answer’s weight by distinguishing accepted agreement from a binding condition to answer every further question.
text: The Devil in the physical position of your Vishuddha can appear in linking an answer to further obligation. Justice in energy supports a wish to match a question with actual agreement rather than attribute extra meaning to words. The Hierophant in emotions brings weight to respectful speech. You can take openness seriously and quietly expand it into unlimited debt. The form retains significance when what was promised and what needs asking separately are understood.

For example, “Just say what you think” receives an honest answer, followed by “Now you have started, explain everything”. One agreement has become grounds for more compulsory details. **Openness having weight does not make it unlimited**. You can name a new question and hear readiness instead of treating earlier words as permission to ask without end. Respect for the answer remains genuine. A specific boundary makes neither the first admission deceitful nor every further exchange closed.

Formality appears if a boundary declares every question disrespectful. The binding condition then reverses direction while an actual request remains unheard. Constructive Justice helps distinguish a right to ask from a commitment already accepted. You can honour words and hear clarification; respect requires neither disclosing everything personal nor prohibiting interest after an initial answer, provided the question remains a genuine proposal rather than an announced debt.
